## Incident Report — 2022-01-07 Traffic Analysis Exercise

**Victim host**
- IPv4: `192.168.1.216`
- MAC: `9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9`
- Windows hostname: `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2` (confirmed via Kerberos `CNameString` machine account `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2$`; NBNS broadcasts the same host as `DESKTOP-GXNYNO2`/`SPOONWATCH`)
- Logged-in user: `steve.smith` (Kerberos AS-REQ/TGS-REQ `CNameString`, domain `spoonwatch.net`, DC `SPOONWATCH-DC` at `192.168.1.2`)

**Malware family: Vidar Stealer — attribution is behavioral, not signature-confirmed** (no IDS/Suricata alert file was present in the evidence directory; only the pcap and tshark-exported HTTP objects were provided).

Behavioral basis for the Vidar call:
- The host makes a direct, DNS-less TCP connection to `2.56.57.108:80` (no prior A-record lookup for this IP anywhere in the capture — the address is hardcoded in the binary).
- It downloads seven files from `/osk/*.jpg` that are served as `image/jpeg` but are actually Windows PE32 DLLs: `sqlite3.dll`, `nss3.dll`, `freebl3.dll`, `softokn3.dll`, `mozglue.dll`, `msvcp140.dll`, `vcruntime140.dll` (confirmed via PDB/import strings in each). This is Vidar's well-documented technique of fetching its Firefox-NSS/SQLite dependency DLLs disguised as jpg images before it can decrypt browser credential stores.
- It then POSTs a file `_5861695120.zip` to `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` (Content-Length 379629, matches the exported `osk` object exactly). The zip contains `autofill/`, `cc/`, `cookies/` (per-browser: Google Chrome_Default, Microsoft Edge_Default/Network), `outlook.txt`, `passwords.txt`, `screenshot.jpg`, `system.txt` — this is Vidar's standard stealer-log folder layout.
- Every request to the C2 carries the fingerprint HTTP header set `Accept: text/html, application/xml;q=0.9, ... image/jpeg ...`, `Accept-Language: ru-RU,ru;q=0.9,en;q=0.8`, `Cache-Control: no-cache`, multipart boundary `1BEF0A57BE110FD467A` — a known Vidar network signature.
- C2 server banner: `Apache/2.4.12 (Win32) OpenSSL/1.0.1m PHP/5.3.29 mod_wsgi/4.4.11 Python/2.7.10`.

## Indicators of Compromise

**C2 endpoint**
- `2.56.57.108:80` — HTTP, all malicious traffic to/from the victim (frames 1498–4830+)

**URLs (fake-image DLL downloads + stealer-log upload, all on the C2 above)**
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//1.jpg` through `/osk//7.jpg` (GET responses deliver PE DLLs mislabeled `image/jpeg`)
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk//main.php`
- `http://2.56.57.108/osk/` (POST — final exfil upload)

**No malicious domain observed** — the C2 was contacted by bare IP with no preceding DNS query.

**Files transferred (all recovered from `2.56.57.108`)**

| File | SHA256 | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `1(1).jpg` (sqlite3.dll) | `16574f51785b0e2fc29c2c61477eb47bb39f714829999511dc8952b43ab17660` | Fetched as `1.jpg`, actually PE32 DLL |
| `2(1).jpg` (freebl3.dll/nss3.dll) | `a770ecba3b08bbabd0a567fc978e50615f8b346709f8eb3cfacf3faab24090ba` | Fetched as `2.jpg`, actually PE32 DLL |
| `3(1).jpg` (mozglue.dll) | `3fe6b1c54b8cf28f571e0c5d6636b4069a8ab00b4f11dd842cfec00691d0c9cd` | Fetched as `3.jpg`, actually PE32 DLL |
| `4(1).jpg` (msvcp140/vcruntime140) | `334e69ac9367f708ce601a6f490ff227d6c20636da5222f148b25831d22e13d4` | Fetched as `4.jpg`, actually PE32 DLL |
| `5(1).jpg` (sqlite3.dll variant) | `e2935b5b28550d47dc971f456d6961f20d1633b4892998750140e0eaa9ae9d78` | Fetched as `5.jpg`, actually PE32 DLL |
| `6(1).jpg` (freebl3.dll/softokn3.dll) | `43536adef2ddcc811c28d35fa6ce3031029a2424ad393989db36169ff2995083` | Fetched as `6.jpg`, actually PE32 DLL |
| `7(1).jpg` (vcruntime140.dll) | `c40bb03199a2054dabfc7a8e01d6098e91de7193619effbd0f142a7bf031c14d` | Fetched as `7.jpg`, actually PE32 DLL |
| `osk` (exfil upload, filename `_5861695120.zip`) | `1ecee6ff37e03c1160b8bf66d5ca8dc784e0b35fb9fd105f0964b314d310c07f` | Stealer log: browser autofill, cookies, credit card data, Outlook data, saved passwords, desktop screenshot, system info — uploaded via POST to `/osk/` |

**Benign context (not indicators)** — Microsoft telemetry/update/CDN infrastructure (`*.events.data.microsoft.com`, `windowsupdate.com`, `client.wns.windows.com`, `bing.com`, `api.msn.com`), internal AD/Kerberos/LDAP/SMB traffic with the domain controller `192.168.1.2` (`spoonwatch.net`), and SSDP/mDNS/LLMNR broadcast noise.

**Incident summary:** The Windows workstation `DESKTOP-GXMYNO2` (`192.168.1.216`, MAC `9c:5c:8e:32:58:f9`), logged in as domain user `steve.smith` on the `spoonwatch.net` AD domain, was infected with Vidar Stealer. The malware connected directly to its C2 at `2.56.57.108:80`, downloaded its required Firefox-NSS and SQLite DLL dependencies disguised as `.jpg` images under `/osk/`, then harvested browser autofill data, cookies, saved credit-card entries, saved passwords, Outlook data, a desktop screenshot, and system information, packaging it as `_5861695120.zip` and exfiltrating it back to the same C2 via HTTP POST. No delivery mechanism (initial infection vector) is visible in this capture — the traffic begins directly at the C2 beaconing stage.
